protocol.title: Two-Dimensional Protein Separation with Advanced Sample and Buffer Isolation Using Microfluidic Valves
protocol.platform: Continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic chip with pneumatic monolith valves (pressure-driven + electrokinetic)
protocol.objective: Integrate isoelectric focusing (IEF, 1st dimension) with capillary gel electrophoresis (CGE) or capillary zone electrophoresis (CZE, 2nd dimension) using active pneumatic microvalve control to isolate incompatible separation buffers, prevent peak interdiffusion, and achieve 2D protein separation on-chip within 10 min

fabrication.master: Photolithography using AZ-4620 (positive) and SU-8 50 (negative) photoresist
fabrication.separation_channel_mold: 150 um wide, 12 um high; heated to 150 C for 30 min (round-shaped)
fabrication.valve_control_channel_mold: 300 um wide, 50 um high (square cross section)
fabrication.silane_treatment: 30 min hexamethyldisilazane vapor to prevent adhesion to silicone rubber
fabrication.pdms_mixing_ratio: 10:1 (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); degassed at 5 psi vacuum
fabrication.bonding: Oxygen plasma (Harrick Scientific); control layer bonded to separation layer, then onto PDMS-on-glass substrate
fabrication.control_channel_access: 1/16-in. o.d. metal syringe needle (Hamilton); 1/16-in. Teflon tubing pressure lines

valves.notes: Right valves (3,4) isolate IEF channel from CGE channel during CE media loading. Left valves (1,2) isolate CGE gel during IEF sample injection. Both sets closed to trap peak transfer region.

static_coating.polymerization_condition: N2 purge, 5 psi vacuum chamber, 30 min

dynamic_coating.purpose: Further minimise protein adsorption and suppress EOF

surface_treatment.outcome: Protein adsorption undetectable by fluorescence microscopy for duration of single 2D separation experiment

ief_sample_solution.notes: 1% methylcellulose suppresses EOF; IEF linearity experiment uses 3% methylcellulose and 5% ampholyte

labeled_proteins.labels: Fluorescein or Alexa Fluor 488 (attached to lysine residues; proteins may acquire multiple dye molecules and multiple pI values)

ief_markers.detection: Fluorescence microscopy, ex 330-340 nm, em 415-500 nm

reagents.anolyte: 0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5; contains same methylcellulose concentration as IEF sample
reagents.catholyte: 0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5; contains same methylcellulose concentration as IEF sample

cge_gel_buffer.composition: 90% SDS 14-200 gel buffer (Beckman Coulter, Fullerton, CA) + 1% methylcellulose
cge_gel_buffer.notes: Same methylcellulose concentration used across all solutions for better mixing in peak transfer region

cze_buffer.notes: Used in IEF-CZE arm (separate experiment); structurally identical protocol to IEF-CGE arm

steps.name: Surface passivation - static polyacrylamide coating
steps.notes: Coat PDMS channel with 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate adhesion promoter, then introduce acrylamide + TEMED + APS under N2 purge (5 psi vacuum) for 30 min. Follow with 0.5% methylcellulose dynamic coating. Reduces protein adsorption to undetectable levels.

steps.name: CGE gel buffer loading into second-dimension channel
steps.valve_state: right valves (3,4) closed at 80 psi to isolate IEF channel
steps.notes: CE media loaded into 25 mm CGE channel without contaminating the 10 mm IEF channel. Methylcellulose concentration matched across all solutions.

steps.name: IEF sample preparation
steps.notes: Ampholyte + glycerol/methylcellulose carrier prepared first, then all four labeled protein samples combined and merged into the carrier. All four proteins loaded simultaneously.

steps.name: IEF sample loading and reservoir buffer replacement
steps.valve_state: left valves (1,2) closed to isolate CGE gel; right valves (3,4) opened
steps.notes: Ampholyte-sample mixture injected into IEF channel at low pressure. Reservoirs replaced: anolyte (0.1 M acetic acid, pH 2.5) at anode; catholyte (0.5% ammonium hydroxide, pH 10.5) at cathode.

steps.name: IEF focusing (1st dimension)
steps.notes: pH 3-10 gradient established. Proteins focus to stationary pI bands. EOF slowly mobilises peaks from anode to cathode. IEF steady state confirmed by monitoring current through channel. Equilibration 2 orders of magnitude faster than CIEF in 25-50 cm capillaries (~30 min).

steps.name: IEF peak detection and QC gate
steps.camera: Thermoelectrically cooled CCD (Cooke Co., Auburn Hills, MI)

steps.name: Peak isolation by valve closure
steps.valve_state: both valve sets (1,2 and 3,4) closed at 80 psi
steps.notes: Target protein peaks physically isolated in 3 mm peak transfer region. No protein intercontamination observed after 30 min. Dead volume 0.1 nL is much smaller than commercial microvalves (10-100 nL). Symmetric channel layout prevents valve operation from mobilising proteins in transfer region.

steps.name: CGE buffer equilibration
steps.notes: Buffer ions diffuse into peak transfer region for 30 s to prevent abrupt conductivity jump before CE field application. Protein diffusion negligible (large MW, slow diffusion constant relative to buffer ions). Small-MW ampholyte co-isolated with proteins eluted rapidly by electrophoresis.

steps.name: CGE separation (2nd dimension)
steps.stacking_mechanism: Proteins entering high-conductivity gel buffer from low-conductivity ampholyte experience sudden velocity decrease at buffer boundary; narrows launching band

electrophoretic_mobilities.notes: Ovalbumin (45 kDa) higher mobility than GFP (26 kDa) due to charge-to-mass ratio dependence in non-denaturing CGE

steps.notes: Stacking ensures 1st and 2nd dimension separations are independent (verified by reversing IEF orientation, Figure 5).

steps.name: CGE fluorescence readout and QC gate
steps.readout: Electropherograms at end of 25 mm CGE channel; fluorescence intensity vs. time
steps.expected_elution_order: Ovalbumin before GFP (higher charge-to-mass ratio, higher mobility)

ief_cze_arm.note: The IEF-CZE (capillary zone electrophoresis) arm is structurally identical to the IEF-CGE arm above. CGE_GelBuffer is replaced by CZE_Buffer (0.375 M Tris-Cl, pH 8.6, 0.1% methylcellulose) at Steps S2 and S8. Electric field in 2nd dimension: 250 V/cm. Stacking still occurs at the liquid-liquid conductivity boundary. CE shows higher resolution and faster separation than CGE (lower viscosity, faster liquid-liquid interface mixing). Independence of 1st and 2nd dimension verified by reversing IEF orientation (catholyte/anolyte swap, Figure 5a/5b). A separate .bs file should encode the IEF-CZE arm with CZE_Buffer substituted for CGE_GelBuffer.

ief_linearity.pH_gradient: pH 3-10 established in 10 mm PDMS channel at 500 V/cm
ief_linearity.nonlinearity: Observed at high pH side due to ampholyte mixture optimised for fused-silica capillary (different EOF characteristics from PDMS surface)
ief_linearity.mitigation: Adding 8.1-9.8 ampholyte to wide-range 3-10 ampholyte shifts peaks at high pH side; further study required

peak_isolation.selectability: Any single pI region can be isolated and sent to 2nd dimension by valve operation (Figure 5c: GFP isolated independently)
peak_isolation.multi_transfer: Multiple regions can be transferred simultaneously by integrating additional valve sets

results.validation_method: Reversing IEF orientation (catholyte/anolyte swap); 2nd-dimension separation unaffected by 1st-dimension peak order

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Surface coating, CGE buffer loading, IEF sample prep and loading, IEF focusing, IEF detection

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: Peak isolation, CGE buffer equilibration, CGE separation, CGE detection
